name: Iznik tiles
summary: Painted wall tiles that the Iznik kilns made for the Ottoman court. A white quartz body takes a white slip, a free painting of flowers in cobalt, turquoise, green and raised red, and a clear glaze.

philosophy.core_thesis: A court tile is a garden in glaze: the painter shows tulips, carnations and leaves in clear colours on a white ground, and the glaze gives them depth.
design_principles: Cover the quartz body with a white slip, then paint the design on the slip under a clear glaze.
Draw the outline in black or cobalt first, then fill the shapes with flat colour.
Paint the flowers of the court garden: tulip, carnation, hyacinth, rose and the long saz leaf.
Put the raised red, made of bole clay, on a flower only after about 1560; keep it 0.1 to 0.3 mm thick.
Add emerald green after 1567; before that use only cobalt, turquoise, purple and black.
Set the tiles in a square repeat of 25 cm and fit a border and a corner tile to each panel.
Cover a whole wall or lunette over a window, with the design running over the joints.
Leave a white ground between the shapes; let the white carry about one third of the surface.
anti_patterns: A body of ordinary red clay under the slip
A flat printed pattern with no brush line
Gold and lustre in the painting
A dull red that does not stand in relief
Figures of people and animals on the tile

form.shape: Square wall tiles in sets, tile panels and lunettes for mosques and palaces, border tiles with a saz-leaf frieze, and tile friezes for tombs.
form.profile: A flat plane with a very slight relief where the red bole stands above the glaze; the tile is thin and light for a wall.
form.foot_and_rim: The back is rough and unglazed with a mortar key; edges are square and cut after the biscuit firing to fit tight joints.
form.proportion: A wall tile is about 25 cm square and 10 to 15 mm thick; panels cover many square metres.
rules: Paint the picture across several tiles and cut the tiles to the pattern.
Keep the white slip and the clear glaze thin, about 0.5 mm each.
Fit the repeat of the flowers to the tile joints.

bodies.rule: Use a white stonepaste of ground quartz, glass frit and a little clay. It is hard and white like porcelain, but it contains no kaolin.

methods: pressing the tile in a flat mould
drying the tile in the shade
painting from a pricked paper cartoon
forming.joins: Tiles are set in lime mortar on the wall, with joints of 1 to 2 mm.
forming.details: Pinprick marks of the cartoon, a clear brush line, a fine crackle in the glaze and a slight blur at the edge of the colours.

glaze.pattern: Tulips, carnations, hyacinths and saz leaves in cobalt, turquoise, green and raised red on a white slip ground.
glaze.gloss: Bright and glassy, about 80 to 95 GU.
glaze.wear: The glaze keeps its shine for centuries; the red crazes in time, and old tiles show fine crackle.

palette.strategy: A white ground with cobalt and turquoise; the tomato red from 1560 and the emerald green from 1567 give the peak colours.

firing.kiln: A kiln with saggars in the town of Iznik, fired with wood.
processes: biscuit firing of the pressed tile
slip and painting on the biscuit
firing.scale: Iznik kilns made large sets of tiles for imperial buildings in Istanbul, often to one order of the court.
firing.signs: Raised red under the glaze, a fine crackle, a blur of the blue at the outline, and stilt marks on the back.

pieces.form: Square tile of 25 cm with a blue tulip and a turquoise saz leaf on white
Mosque wall panel with tulips, carnations and a raised red on a white ground
Border band with a repeat of leaves in cobalt and turquoise
Lunette above a window with a vase of flowers and a cypress

positive: tulip and carnation in cobalt and turquoise
fine crackle in a clear glaze

canonical_works.work: Tile panels of the Rüstem Pasha Mosque, Istanbul
Tile panels of the mausoleum of Süleyman I, Istanbul
Tile lining of the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, Istanbul

evidence.title: Iznik tiles in the Rüstem Pasha Mosque

emotion.target_response: A bright, calm delight: the viewer stands in a garden of flowers that never fade and feels the wealth of a court.

use_cases: a mosque or palace wall in Ottoman tile
a floral tile pattern brief with a white ground
a museum label on Ottoman court ceramics
avoid_when: the brief wants a geometric cut mosaic
the brief needs a plain single-colour tile
the brief is for a modern minimal room

modifiers.how: Change to glazed tiles in one colour, cut into small shapes, and set them in a star pattern.
Change to a tin-glazed earthenware tile and paint one blue scene across a panel.
